internal_alignment: Equal versus unequal parts (same size, not same shape); halves (2 equal parts, 2 halves make the whole, half of); fourths and quarters (4 equal parts, 4 fourths make the whole, fourth of, quarter of); equal shares can look different (halves cut vertically, horizontally, or diagonally; fourths as strips or as a grid); more equal shares make smaller shares of the same whole. Internal record only; the printable answer key carries no standards codes or references.
model_accuracy: Every division verified mathematically before rendering: circle halves are 180 degree diameter sectors at vertical, horizontal, and diagonal angles; rectangle halves are equal halves by area including diagonal triangles (each exactly half the rectangle area); fourths are equal strips (width/4 each), equal grid quarters, and 90 degree circle quarters; unequal splits are genuinely unequal (off-center chord with minor cap under 40 percent of the circle area, 60/120 wedges, 30/70 rectangle split). Page 1 answers: tick, cross, tick, cross, tick, cross in shape order (circle halves equal; chord split unequal; rectangle halves equal; narrow/wide rectangle unequal; rectangle strips equal; circle wedges unequal). Page 2: color 1 half, either half right. Page 3: join opposite dots through the center (matching top/bottom dots for strips), color 1 fourth. Page 4: pairs 1, 2, and 3 tick (halves vertical/horizontal; halves vertical/diagonal; fourths strips/grid); pair 4 no tick (halves versus fourths). Page 5: the smaller share in each row is the fourth (quarter).
pack: Grade 1 Math: Halves and Fourths of Shapes

pages_detail.activities: Worked equal/unequal pair (equal circle halves beside an off-center chord split); six split shapes in two rows of three with a tick/cross response box beneath each
pages_detail.title: Equal Parts or Not?

pages_detail.activities: Worked whole circle beside its two halves (2 halves make the whole; each part is half of the circle); four large shapes split vertically, horizontally, and diagonally to color 1 half from
answers: Color 1 half of each shape; either half is right
pages_detail.title: Halves

pages_detail.activities: Worked grid example with one fourth colored beside a demonstration circle with dashed lines joining opposite dots through the center; four wholes with guide dots at the exact division points to join and then color 1 fourth from
answers: Join opposite dots through the center; color 1 fourth of each shape
pages_detail.title: Fourths

pages_detail.activities: Four pairs of identical wholes partitioned differently (rectangle halves vertical/horizontal; circle halves vertical/diagonal; rectangle fourths strips/grid; halves versus fourths contrast); color one part in each shape and tick if both shapes show halves or both show fourths; reminder line that equal shares can look different
pages_detail.title: Same Share, Different Look

pages_detail.activities: Two rows of identical wholes (circles, then rectangles) in halves and fourths with share captions (1 half of, 1 quarter of); color 1 share in each shape and tick the smaller share in the box beneath it
answers: Smaller share in each row: the fourth (quarter)
pages_detail.title: More Parts, Smaller Pieces
